question: What is concessional posting?
text: Concessional posting lets a prospective corps member be deployed on marital or health grounds. It is applied for during online registration, not afterwards.

question: What documents do married women need for posting to their husband's state?
text: A married female prospective corps member who wants posting to her husband's state of domicile uploads, during online registration: her marriage certificate, evidence of change of name and the husband's place of domicile, and the husband's means of identification such as a driving licence or national ID card.

question: Can I be posted based on a health condition?
text: A prospective corps member with a serious health challenge should state their true health status during registration to allow concessional deployment, and upload a medical report from a federal or state general hospital along with the doctor's details.

question: How do I relocate to my husband's state after deployment?
text: To relocate from the current state of deployment to a husband's state of domicile, submit an application attaching the marriage certificate, newspaper publication for change of name, a letter from the husband's employer, and the husband's means of identification.

question: What should I do before registering?
text: Before registering, Nigerian-trained graduates should verify that their details are correct on the NYSC portal's Senate list verification page, and have a functional email address ready. Only those whose names appear on the Senate or Academic Board approved result list submitted by their institution can register.

question: What are the steps of online registration?
text: Online registration runs in this order: create an account with a functional email address, activate it through the link emailed to you, fill in your details, capture biometrics in person, upload a clear off-white background passport photograph, preview the form for errors, accept the terms, upload a scanned or digital signature, submit, and keep your login details for later use.

question: Do part-time graduates need to register on the NYSC portal?
text: Yes. Part-time graduates register when the portal opens so they can print their exclusion letter from their dashboard.

question: What can I do on my dashboard after registration?
text: Self-services available on the dashboard after registration include: correcting name spelling, date of birth, course of study, class of degree and qualification; applying for relocation after camp; printing call-up, exclusion and relocation letters; printing the place of primary assignment letter after camp reposting; and printing leave approval letters.

question: How do I correct a mistake in my name?
text: To correct a name spelling or rearrangement, log in to your dashboard, click Apply for Name Correction, fill the required fields and place the request, then wait for approval. NYSC does not approve adding or removing names — only fixing an existing one.

question: How do I correct my course of study, class of degree or qualification?
text: Corrections to course of study, class of degree or qualification are all requested from the dashboard by selecting the correct value and sending the request. Approval is granted strictly by your institution's Student Affairs Officer, not by NYSC.

question: How do I correct my date of birth?
text: To correct a date of birth, get a 19- or 20-digit WAEC verification pin from any First Bank branch, then on your dashboard enter the pin, WAEC type, exam year and examination number, and verify before submitting. The gap between your date of graduation and your WAEC exam must be at least four years.

question: How do I correct my date of birth after an exemption certificate has been issued?
text: If an exemption certificate has already been printed, collect the original from your institution and apply to your Student Affairs Officer, who forwards it to NYSC headquarters. The school returns the original exemption certificate and a photocopy of the WAEC or GCE certificate, after which NYSC enables the date of birth change on your dashboard when the portal opens.

question: How do I correct my date of graduation if I was wrongly exempted?
text: If you were wrongly exempted, collect the original exemption certificate from your institution and complain to the Student Affairs Officer, who writes a signed letter to NYSC headquarters stating the correct date of graduation and returns the original certificate. NYSC then enables revalidation when the portal opens.

question: How do I collect my exemption certificate?
text: Locally trained graduates who are exempted from service collect their exemption certificate from their institution, and corrections are only allowed within three months of online registration. Foreign-trained graduates go to NYSC headquarters with their original documents for clearance and collection.

question: Do foreign graduates need to bring documents to camp?
text: Yes. Foreign-trained graduates who registered online must bring to camp all original documents as uploaded, plus a translated version of the certificate, and must be cleared by the verification officer before leaving camp for any reason. Failing to do so cancels the registration and no place of primary assignment is given.

question: Do medical graduates need to bring their practice licence to camp?
text: Yes. Prospective corps members in the medical profession must bring their practising licence to the orientation camp.

question: What do I do if my name is not on the Senate list?
text: If your name is not found on the Senate list, or your matriculation or JAMB number already exists, contact your institution — NYSC cannot resolve these directly.

question: When does registration open?
text: NYSC publishes the mobilization timetable for each service year batch on its official website. Because dates change every batch, check the current timetable at nysc.gov.ng/mobtable.html rather than relying on remembered dates.

question: What is SAED?
text: SAED stands for Skills Acquisition and Entrepreneurship Development. It is the NYSC department that runs skill training for corps members, sets the curriculum for the in-camp skill acquisition exercise, attaches corps members to organisations for training in specific skill sets, and helps them access funding opportunities.

question: Do I learn a skill during camp?
text: Yes. There is an in-camp skill acquisition exercise with a standard national curriculum, and corps members are sensitized in camp to enrol in the wider skill acquisition and entrepreneurship programme that continues after camp.

question: What do I do if I lose my NYSC certificate?
text: NYSC does not reissue a lost certificate. The Certification Division issues a Letter of Confirmation in lieu of a lost Certificate of National Service, and the Exemption Division does the same for a lost Certificate of Exemption or Letter of Exclusion.

question: What happens if I don't collect my certificate after passing out?
text: Certificates of National Service that are not claimed are returned to NYSC Headquarters two weeks after passing-out and are kept in the Certification Division.

question: What is the difference between a certificate of national service, exemption and exclusion?
text: NYSC issues three instruments: a Certificate of National Service to corps members who complete service, a Certificate of Exemption to eligible full-time graduates who are exempted, and a Letter of Exclusion to eligible part-time graduates. Exemption certificates are collected from your institution (or NYSC Headquarters for foreign-trained graduates), while exclusion letters are printed online.

question: Can I get a temporary letter of exclusion?
text: No. NYSC no longer issues temporary letters of exclusion — original letters of exclusion are issued through the NYSC online platform.

question: Who do I contact about my certificate?
text: The Corps Certification Department publishes a hotline for complaints and enquiries about certificates: 08034313026.

question: Am I insured during service?
text: Yes. Corps members are covered by a group life insurance arrangement. The Corps Insurance Division processes payments for corps members who suffer permanent disability, and in the event of death the registered next of kin is traced and paid the entitlements.

question: Can I claim back money I spent on medical treatment?
text: Yes. The Corps Health Service Division prepares and processes medical refund bills for corps members and liaises with the accounts department for payment.

question: What welfare issues can NYSC help me with?
text: The Corps Welfare Division handles allowances, leave (sick, maternity and absence), accident cases, benefits, permission to travel abroad, and cases of theft or harassment.

question: Can I take leave during service?
text: Yes. Leave — including sick leave, maternity leave and leave of absence — is handled by the Corps Welfare Division, and approved leave letters are printed from your dashboard on the NYSC portal.

question: Can I travel abroad during my service year?
text: Permission to travel abroad during the service year is a welfare matter handled by the Corps Welfare Division, so it must be formally applied for rather than assumed.

question: What do I do if I have a problem with my employer at my PPA?
text: The Investigation branch of the Corps Inspectorate handles matters of misconduct and disputes between corps members and their employers or NYSC officials, with the aim of resolving the differences.

question: What happens if a corps member breaks the rules?
text: Disciplinary cases start at the state secretariat and follow the procedures laid down in the NYSC bye-law. The Corps Merit and Discipline Division reviews and ratifies the recommendations of state corps disciplinary committees.

question: What is the President's NYSC Honours Award?
text: The President's NYSC Honours Award recognises outstanding corps members. Nomination guidelines are set by the Merit branch of the Corps Merit and Discipline Division, which also organises the award ceremony. State Honours Awards are separately given at passing-out to members who excelled across camp, primary assignment, CDS and winding-up.

question: Do corps members work for INEC during elections?
text: Yes. NYSC has a memorandum of understanding with the Independent National Electoral Commission, and a dedicated unit within Corps Welfare and Health Services handles all INEC-related matters affecting corps members.

question: How much should a cybercafé charge me to register?
text: Accredited cybercafé operators must not charge more than N2,000 for registration services rendered to prospective corps members, whether Nigerian or foreign-trained. Note that biometric capture must still be done by you in person, never by proxy.

question: Are cybercafés allowed to help with NYSC registration?
text: Yes, but only accredited ones. NYSC registers and accredits cybercafé operators to weed out quacks and reduce registration errors, issuing a certificate after document verification and premises inspection.

question: Is there an NYSC mobile app?
text: Yes. NYSC publishes an official mobile app on the Google Play Store, linked from the quick links section of nysc.gov.ng.

question: What are the official NYSC social media channels?
text: NYSC's official channels are Facebook (officialnysc), X (officialnyscng), Instagram (officialnyscng), TikTok (nyscofficial), YouTube (nyscdhq1), a WhatsApp channel, and Telegram (official_nysc). Announcements that do not come from these channels or from nysc.gov.ng should be treated with caution.

question: Where can I see what happens at camp?
text: NYSC runs a camp activities portal at campactivity.nyscselfservice.com.ng showing activities across orientation camps.

question: What is PPA?
text: Place of Primary Assignment (PPA) is where a corps member is posted to work for the rest of the service year after orientation camp.

question: What is CDS?
text: Community Development Service (CDS) is the segment of the service year where corps members carry out projects that address needs in their host community.

question: What is SAED?
text: Skills Acquisition and Entrepreneurship Development (SAED) is the NYSC programme that trains corps members in vocational and entrepreneurial skills during and after orientation camp.

question: What is POP / passing out parade?
text: Passing Out Parade (POP) is the ceremony that marks the end of the NYSC service year, when corps members are formally discharged.

question: What is orientation camp?
text: Orientation camp is the three-week compulsory residential programme that begins the NYSC service year for all mobilised graduates.

question: What is redeployment?
text: Redeployment is the process of moving a corps member's posting from one state to another for an approved reason.

question: What is a call-up letter?
text: A call-up letter is the official document issued by NYSC that confirms a prospective corps member's mobilisation and states their assigned state of deployment.

question: What is the NYSC allowance commonly called?
text: The NYSC allowance is commonly called "allawee" in Nigerian slang.
